runbooks.title: Connect to the office Wi-Fi
runbooks.summary: Join the staff Wi-Fi network Meridian-Staff on a work laptop or phone in any Meridian office.
steps: Open your Wi-Fi settings and choose the network Meridian-Staff.
When asked to sign in, use your work email address and your normal work sign-in.
Accept the certificate named meridian-radius if your device asks about it.
If the network does not appear, turn Wi-Fi off and on again and move closer to the centre of the floor.
Still stuck after two tries? Post in #it-help and say which office and floor you are on.

runbooks.title: Get a visitor onto the guest Wi-Fi
runbooks.summary: Give a visitor internet access with a one-day code for the Meridian-Guest network.
steps: Ask the visitor to choose the network Meridian-Guest on their device.
Open the Front Desk page on the intranet and select Guest Wi-Fi code.
Enter the visitor's name and the date of the visit. The page shows a code that lasts until midnight.
The visitor types the code on the sign-in page that opens when they join the network.
Guest Wi-Fi reaches the internet only. It cannot reach printers, file shares or internal sites.

runbooks.title: Set up the VPN app for the first time
runbooks.summary: Install and sign in to the Meridian VPN app so you can reach internal sites from outside the office.
steps: Open Self Service on a Mac, or Company Portal on Windows, and install Meridian VPN.
Start the app. The portal address is already filled in; do not change it.
Select Connect and sign in with your work account in the browser window that opens.
Wait for the shield icon to turn green. That means the VPN is on.
The VPN turns itself off after 12 hours. Select Connect again when you need it.

runbooks.title: VPN is connected but internal sites don't load
runbooks.summary: What to check when the VPN shows connected and the intranet or other internal sites still time out.
steps: Check that the shield icon is green and not grey or amber.
Select Disconnect, wait ten seconds, then select Connect again.
Turn off any personal VPN or ad-blocking app on the laptop; two VPNs cannot run together.
On hotel or cafe Wi-Fi, open any normal website first and accept the network's sign-in page, then reconnect the VPN.
Restart the laptop if internal sites still fail.
If it still fails after a restart, post in #it-help with the name of the site you cannot open.

runbooks.title: Add an office printer on a Mac
runbooks.summary: Add the office follow-me printer queue to a work Mac.
steps: Connect to Meridian-Staff Wi-Fi or the VPN.
Open Self Service and select Printers, then Install next to Meridian-Print.
Open any document, choose Print, and pick Meridian-Print.
Walk to any office printer and tap your badge to release the job.
Jobs that are not released are deleted after 24 hours.

runbooks.title: Add an office printer on Windows
runbooks.summary: Add the office follow-me printer queue to a work Windows laptop.
steps: Connect to Meridian-Staff Wi-Fi or the VPN.
Open Company Portal, search for Meridian-Print and select Install.
Restart any app that was open, then choose Print and pick Meridian-Print.
Walk to any office printer and tap your badge to release the job.
Jobs that are not released are deleted after 24 hours.

runbooks.title: Scan a document to your email
runbooks.summary: Scan paper on an office printer and receive it as a PDF in your work mailbox.
steps: Tap your badge on the printer.
Choose Scan, then Scan to my email.
Put the pages face up in the top feeder, or one page face down on the glass.
Press Start. The PDF arrives in your work mailbox within a few minutes.
Scans go only to your own work address. To send one to somebody else, forward the email.

runbooks.title: Book a meeting room
runbooks.summary: Reserve a meeting room from Google Calendar and check in at the room's panel.
steps: Create the event in Google Calendar.
Select Rooms, pick your office, and choose a room that shows as free.
Save the event. The room accepts by itself if it is free.
When the meeting starts, tap Check in on the panel beside the door.
A room that nobody checks in to within 10 minutes is released for others.

runbooks.title: Start a video call in a meeting room
runbooks.summary: Use the room's screen, camera and microphone for a Google Meet call.
steps: Book the room in the calendar event; the call then appears on the room's touch panel.
Tap the meeting name on the touch panel to join.
To show your laptop, join the same call on the laptop and select Present now. Mute the laptop's microphone and speakers first.
Use the touch panel to change the volume or turn the room camera off.
Tap Leave on the panel when you finish so the room is free for the next group.

runbooks.title: Set up work email on your phone
runbooks.summary: Add your work Google account to a phone inside the managed work profile.
steps: On Android, install Intune Company Portal; on an iPhone, install Self Service from the App Store.
Open it and follow the steps to enrol the phone. This creates a separate work profile.
Install Gmail and Google Calendar from the work profile's app list.
Open Gmail and sign in with your work account.
Work data stays in the work profile. IT cannot see your personal apps, photos or messages.

runbooks.title: Turn on an out-of-office reply
runbooks.summary: Set an automatic reply in Gmail for days when you are away.
steps: Open Gmail in a browser and select the gear icon, then See all settings.
Scroll to Vacation responder and select Vacation responder on.
Set the first and last day, and write a short message that says who covers for you.
Tick Only send a response to people in Meridian if outside senders should not get it.
Select Save changes. The reply stops by itself after the last day.

runbooks.title: Use the standard email signature
runbooks.summary: Create a Gmail signature that follows Meridian's template.
steps: Open the Brand page on the intranet and copy the signature template.
In Gmail, open Settings, See all settings, and scroll to Signature.
Select Create new, paste the template, and replace the sample name, title and office with your own.
Under Signature defaults, choose the signature for new emails and for replies.
Select Save changes. Do not add images, quotes or extra colours.

runbooks.title: Share a Google Drive file with someone outside Meridian
runbooks.summary: The rules and steps for sharing a file or folder with a customer or partner.
steps: Check the file's label first. Files labelled Confidential or Restricted cannot be shared outside the company.
Open the file, select Share, and type the outside person's email address.
Choose Viewer unless they really need to edit, and add an expiry date.
Never use Anyone with the link for work files.
Remove the person from the file when the work is finished.

runbooks.title: Get back a deleted Google Drive file
runbooks.summary: Restore a file you deleted from My Drive within the last 30 days.
steps: Open Google Drive in a browser and select Trash in the left menu.
Find the file. You can sort the list by the date it was put in the trash.
Right-click the file and select Restore. It goes back to the folder it came from.
Files stay in Trash for 30 days and are then removed for good.
For a file deleted more than 30 days ago, or one deleted from a shared drive, post in #it-help; IT may be able to recover it.

runbooks.title: Install approved software
runbooks.summary: Install apps that IT has already approved, without admin rights.
steps: On a Mac, open Self Service. On Windows, open Company Portal.
Search for the app by name, or browse the categories.
Select Install and wait until the status says Installed. Large apps can take 15 minutes.
If the app is not in the list, it is not approved yet. Asking for a new app is a separate request to IT.
Never install work software from a download site or with a personal licence.

runbooks.title: Install operating system updates
runbooks.summary: Run macOS or Windows updates when your laptop asks for them.
steps: Save your work and plug the laptop into power.
On a Mac, open System Settings, General, Software Update. On Windows, open Settings, Windows Update.
Select Update now, or Restart now if the update has already downloaded.
Leave the lid open until the laptop is back at the sign-in screen. This can take 45 minutes.
Updates must be installed within 7 days of the first reminder. After that the laptop restarts by itself outside working hours.

runbooks.title: Laptop is slow: first checks
runbooks.summary: Simple checks to try when a work laptop feels slow or the fan runs all the time.
steps: Restart the laptop. A restart clears most slowdowns.
Close browser tabs you are not using; many open tabs use a lot of memory.
Check free disk space. Below 10 GB free, move large files to Google Drive and empty the trash.
Check that system updates are not waiting to be installed.
If it is still slow after a restart, post in #it-help and say what you were doing when it slowed down.

runbooks.title: Set up your new laptop on day one
runbooks.summary: What happens the first time you switch on a new work laptop, and what you need to do.
steps: Connect the laptop to power and switch it on.
Choose your language and join a Wi-Fi network. At home, use your own Wi-Fi.
Sign in with your work account when the Meridian screen appears. Your manager gave you these details before your first day.
Wait while the laptop installs the standard apps. This takes about 30 minutes; you can keep the lid open and walk away.
When the desktop appears, open Self Service or Company Portal to add any extra approved apps.

runbooks.title: Return or swap equipment
runbooks.summary: How to hand back a laptop, phone or accessory you no longer need.
steps: Back up nothing by hand: work files are already in Google Drive. Move any personal files off the device.
Put the device, its charger and any accessories in one bag or box.
In an office, bring it to the IT desk during desk hours. Working remotely, ask in #it-help for a prepaid shipping label.
IT confirms in the ticket when the device has arrived.
Do not pass equipment directly to a colleague; IT has to wipe and re-assign it first.

runbooks.title: Save and share team logins in the password manager
runbooks.summary: Use Meridian Vault to store logins for shared tools and share them with your team safely.
steps: Open the Meridian Vault browser extension and sign in with your work account.
Select New item, choose Login, and fill in the site, the account name and the secret.
To share it, move the item into your team's shared vault. Everyone in that vault can then use it.
Never send a login in Slack, email or a document.
When someone leaves the team, their access to the shared vault ends by itself.

runbooks.title: Join, create and name Slack channels
runbooks.summary: Find and join channels, and the naming rules for creating a new one.
steps: Select Add channels, then Browse channels, and search by topic or team name.
Select Join on any public channel. Private channels need an invite from a member.
To create a channel, select Add channels, then Create a new channel.
Start the name with a prefix: team- for a team, proj- for a project, help- for a help channel.
Add a one-line description so others can tell what the channel is for.

runbooks.title: Set Slack notifications and quiet hours
runbooks.summary: Choose what Slack notifies you about and pause notifications outside working hours.
steps: Select your picture in Slack, then Preferences, then Notifications.
Under Notify me about, choose Direct messages, mentions and keywords.
Under Notification schedule, set the days and hours when you want to be notified.
For a single channel, open the channel name and choose the bell to mute it or get every message.
To pause everything for a while, select your picture and choose Pause notifications.

runbooks.title: Fix microphone or sound in a video call
runbooks.summary: Checks for when people can't hear you, or you can't hear them, in Google Meet or a Slack huddle.
steps: In the call, open the settings and check which microphone and speaker are selected.
Unplug the headset and plug it in again, or turn a Bluetooth headset off and on.
Check that the browser is allowed to use the microphone: select the lock icon beside the address bar.
Close other call apps; only one app can use the microphone at a time.
Leave the call and join again. If it still fails, restart the laptop.

runbooks.title: Connect a second monitor or a dock
runbooks.summary: Plug a work laptop into a desk monitor or docking station and arrange the screens.
steps: Plug the dock's cable into a USB-C port on the laptop. On desks without a dock, plug the monitor cable straight into the laptop.
Wait ten seconds for the monitor to wake up.
On a Mac, open System Settings, Displays. On Windows, open Settings, System, Display.
Drag the screens into the order they have on your desk, and choose which one is the main screen.
If the monitor stays black, unplug the dock's power cable for ten seconds and try again.

runbooks.title: Order a keyboard, mouse or headset
runbooks.summary: Order standard accessories from the IT catalogue.
steps: Open the IT catalogue on the intranet.
Choose from the standard list: keyboard, mouse, headset, webcam, laptop stand or charger.
Add your office or home delivery address and submit the order.
Standard items need no approval and arrive within 5 working days.
Items that are not on the standard list need your manager's approval in the same form.

runbooks.title: Work from another country for a short time
runbooks.summary: The IT checklist before you travel and work from abroad for up to four weeks.
steps: Tell your manager and record the trip in the People portal at least a week before you leave.
Install any waiting system updates before you travel.
Abroad, always turn on the VPN before you open work tools.
Use hotel or cafe Wi-Fi only with the VPN on, and never use a shared or public computer for work.
Some countries are not allowed for work travel. The People portal shows the list when you record the trip.

runbooks.title: Report a suspicious email
runbooks.summary: Report an email that looks like phishing with the Report button in Gmail.
steps: Do not click links or open attachments in the email.
Open the email in Gmail and select the Report phishing button on the right-hand side.
The email moves out of your inbox and goes to the security team for checking.
You get a reply within one working day that says whether it was safe.
If you already clicked a link or typed anything into a page it opened, say so in #it-help straight away.

runbooks.title: Use a USB drive for work files
runbooks.summary: The rules for removable storage, and how to get an encrypted drive.
steps: Personal USB drives are blocked on work laptops. They charge but do not open.
Order an encrypted Meridian drive from the IT catalogue if you need one.
Plug it in and set a passphrase when the laptop asks. The drive is encrypted from then on.
Never store files labelled Restricted on a removable drive.
Hand the drive back to IT when you no longer need it.

runbooks.title: Sign in to Chrome with your work profile
runbooks.summary: Keep work and personal browsing apart by using a work profile in Chrome.
steps: Open Chrome and select the profile picture at the top right.
Select Add, then Sign in, and use your work account.
Choose Keep work and personal browsing separate when Chrome asks.
Work bookmarks, extensions and saved sites now appear only in the work profile.
Use the profile picture to switch between the two profiles.

runbooks.title: Ask IT for help the right way
runbooks.summary: Where to ask, the IT desk hours, and what to include so a request is solved the first time.
steps: Post in #it-help in Slack. One message per problem.
Say what you were trying to do, what happened instead, and when it started.
Add a screenshot of any error message, and say whether you are in an office or remote.
IT desk hours are 08:00 to 18:00 Berlin time on working days. The IT desk in each office is staffed 10:00 to 15:00.
For anything urgent outside those hours that stops many people working, call the on-call number on the intranet's IT page.
